summary: Defines an UNSELECT command for IMAP4 that closes the current mailbox without expunging it. Some clients need to release resources tied to the selected mailbox without selecting another one, which IMAP4 previously did only through awkward workarounds. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: Closing a folder normally might also throw out messages marked for deletion. This adds a way to just close it and leave everything as it was.

questions: how to close an imap mailbox without expunge
subtitle: Close a mailbox without deleting messages marked for removal.

tldr.problem: IMAP clients sometimes need to release resources tied to a selected mailbox without deleting messages marked for deletion, but IMAP4 only provides awkward workarounds.
tldr.mechanism: The UNSELECT command closes the currently selected mailbox and returns the server to authenticated state, just like CLOSE but without expunging deleted messages.
tldr.outcome: Clients have a clean, standard way to release mailbox resources without accidentally losing messages.

today: RFC 3691 is a Proposed Standard. UNSELECT is now part of the core IMAP protocol and is widely supported by mail servers and clients.

sections.title: Why UNSELECT was needed
sections.content: IMAP clients sometimes need to release server resources associated with a selected mailbox but without switching to a different mailbox. The problem is that the existing CLOSE command permanently removes all messages marked with the backslash-Deleted flag. Before UNSELECT was defined, clients had to use awkward workarounds such as selecting a nonexistent mailbox or reselecting the same mailbox in EXAMINE mode.
sections.plainLanguage: Different programs have different ways they want to close a folder. Sometimes they want to save changes, sometimes they don't. This command lets them just close it with nothing changed.

sections.title: The UNSELECT Command
sections.content: UNSELECT takes no arguments and produces no specific response. It frees the server's resources associated with the selected mailbox and returns the connection to authenticated state. It performs the same actions as CLOSE except that no messages are permanently removed from the mailbox. The command responds with OK when successful, or BAD if no mailbox is selected or if an argument was supplied when none are permitted.
sections.plainLanguage: The command is simple: just type UNSELECT and the server closes the folder without throwing anything away.

sections.title: Implementation requirements
sections.content: Servers that support UNSELECT advertise it with the UNSELECT capability. The command syntax is defined in ABNF and is case-insensitive, like all IMAP commands. UNSELECT is specified as a new form of the command-select production. RFC 3501 defines the base IMAP4rev1 protocol, and RFC 2234 specifies the ABNF notation used here.
sections.plainLanguage: Servers that have this feature tell clients about it up front so they know they can use this command.
